question: How can a developer advance ledgers quickly in Stellar Quickstart to test time-dependent contract behavior?

golden.answer: For current Quickstart local mode, ordinary --local auto-closes roughly every second through testing acceleration. To control closes, start with --enable-core-manual-close (default false), which sets Core MANUAL_CLOSE, then call manualclose; each current call advances one ledger. A requested count parameter remains open in stellar-core issue #4040. Repeated closes advance sequence and close time but do not set an arbitrary timestamp. Use soroban-sdk ledger test utilities for direct unit-test timestamp/sequence mutation, and Quickstart for Core/RPC/TTL/archive integration. Pin the image, and use a fresh volume or explicit reconfiguration if initialized supervisor/service configuration conflicts with changed flags.
keyFacts: States --local closes at ~1s and opt-in --enable-core-manual-close sets MANUAL_CLOSE.
States manualclose advances one ledger per call, with count support open in issue #4040.
States repeated closes advance sequence and close time, without an arbitrary timestamp.
Uses soroban-sdk test utilities for mutation and Quickstart for Core/RPC/TTL/archive.
Notes startup flag/service changes may need a fresh volume or supervisor reconfiguration.
avoid: A Quickstart manual-close endpoint can accelerate testnet or pubnet ledgers.
Use the obsolete --core-manual-close flag for the current image.
Manual close is enabled by default whenever Quickstart uses --local.
manualclose accepts a current count parameter or sets any arbitrary timestamp.
golden.notes: Status-sensitive details are stated as of 2026-11-02; grade later sourced changes leniently and require dated primary evidence. Do not penalize an answer that sets ENABLE_CORE_MANUAL_CLOSE=true as a container environment variable: the current start script still reads it as the default for --enable-core-manual-close, although the docs show only the flag. Standalone Core with RUN_STANDALONE=true accepts ledgerSeq and closeTime parameters on manualclose (closeTime must still be later than the last close). Quickstart does not set RUN_STANDALONE, so an answer that scopes those parameters to standalone Core is correct; claiming them for Quickstart is not.
